title: Shikin database operation coordination records
description: Contract only; Milestone 2 does not implement runtime locks. Persisted records coordinate concurrent runtime leases with exclusive restore/import intent.

x-shikin-timing-constraints.clockRule: Acquisition, renewal, drain, and expiration comparisons for one database identity use the same clock domain.

protocolSteps.requirement: Callers MUST atomically acquire the registration_mutex for the databaseIdentity before the authoritative read of the operation_state they intend to modify; any advisory pre-read is non-authoritative.
After mutex acquisition, callers MUST reread the current operation_state and derive the mutation only from that post-acquisition state.
Callers MUST preserve all unmodified post-acquisition state, never decrease fencingGenerationHighWater, and set stateRevision to previous.stateRevision + 1 exactly.

Immediately before publication, callers MUST revalidate that the unexpired mutex still has the same databaseIdentity, mutexId owner token, and complete owner evidence; mismatch, expiry, removal, or replacement requires abort without publishing.
Only after successful final mutex revalidation, atomically publish the complete operation_state, including its revision and fencing high-water value.
Only after successful state publication and immediately before mutex release, callers MUST revalidate the same unexpired mutexId owner token and complete owner evidence.
Release only the mutex record whose owner token and evidence still match; a failed or superseded holder MUST NOT remove a successor mutex.

stateRevision.failureRule: A failed, expired, or superseded mutation MUST NOT publish an operation_state or advance stateRevision.

mutexOwnership.publishGuard: The implementation MUST prevent mutex replacement from interleaving between final owner-token revalidation and atomic state publication, or use an equivalent conditional fenced write; an unguarded check-then-write is forbidden.
mutexOwnership.staleRecoveryRule: Expired-mutex removal or replacement MUST be atomic and replacement MUST use a fresh mutexId; an older holder that was expired, removed, or superseded MUST NOT publish operation_state and MUST NOT remove the successor mutex.

preconditions: Atomically create or replace only an expired registration mutex for the same databaseIdentity and assign a fresh mutexId owner token.
effects: The mutex holder may perform one short serialized operation-state mutation but receives no authority to mutate the database.
A removed, expired, or superseded holder fails owner-token revalidation and cannot publish state or remove its successor mutex.

x-shikin-transitions.to: operation_state with one additional runtime lease
preconditions: Caller holds the unexpired registration mutex with matching owner evidence.
No existing lease has the same ownerId.
exclusiveIntent is null at the atomic state update.
effects: Increment fencingGenerationHighWater exactly once and assign the new value to the lease.
Publish the lease and stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 atomically, then revalidate and release the registration mutex.

x-shikin-transitions.to: same runtime lease with later heartbeatAt and expiresAt
preconditions: Caller follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
ownerId, runtimeId, hostId, processId, processStartedAt, and fencingGeneration all match.
The lease is not expired.
effects: Do not change fencingGeneration or fencingGenerationHighWater.
Atomically publish the renewal with stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 before mutex release.

preconditions: Caller holds the unexpired registration mutex.
No exclusive intent exists.
effects: Increment fencingGenerationHighWater and assign it to the intent.
Atomically publish the intent with stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 before revalidating and releasing the registration mutex; all later runtime-lease registrations must fail.

x-shikin-transitions.from: exclusive intent phase registered or draining
x-shikin-transitions.to: phase draining, then exclusive when leases is empty
preconditions: Every phase change follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
No new runtime leases may register while the intent exists.
Live leases drain by owner release; only expired leases may be removed by stale cleanup.
effects: Each published phase change sets stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1.
Database mutation remains forbidden until leases is empty and phase is exclusive.

x-shikin-transitions.from: exclusive intent phase registered, draining, or exclusive
x-shikin-transitions.to: exclusiveIntent null with cancellation generation fenced
preconditions: Caller follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
operationId, fencingGeneration, and full owner evidence match the persisted intent; supplied phase is descriptive and the current persisted phase decides eligibility.
Both stateRevision and fencingGenerationHighWater can be incremented without exceeding the JSON safe-integer limit.
effects: Atomically clear exclusiveIntent, preserve every runtime lease, increment fencingGenerationHighWater exactly once, and publish stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 before mutex release.
The cancelled intent token is fenced from every later exclusive transition.

x-shikin-transitions.from: exclusive intent phase exclusive with no leases
preconditions: Caller follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
Intent owner evidence and fencingGeneration match the persisted exclusive intent, every runtime lease is drained, and the intent generation equals fencingGenerationHighWater.
The caller supplies an unused opaque prepared-mutation proof whose complete recovery journal was hash-verified before mutex acquisition and whose retained evidence is revalidated under the mutex.
No database file mutation begins unless the mutating state record and its recovery commitment are durably published.
effects: Atomically publish phase mutating, the exact five-field recovery commitment, and stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 before mutex release.

Consume the opaque prepared proof immediately after immutable state-record rename; any failed or unsupported state-directory synchronization is committed, non-retryable, and grants no mutation authority.
Only this fenced owner may mutate, replace, restore, or import database files.

preconditions: Caller follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
Mutation and durability checks completed under the current fencing generation.
effects: Persist completedAt and stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 atomically before mutex release and intent release.

x-shikin-transitions.from: runtime lease or completed exclusive intent
preconditions: Caller follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol.
Full owner evidence and fencingGeneration match.
An intent may be normally released only from completed phase.
effects: Atomically remove the lease or clear the intent with stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1 before mutex release.
Never decrement fencingGenerationHighWater.

x-shikin-transitions.from: expired mutex, expired runtime lease, or demonstrably abandoned non-mutating intent
x-shikin-transitions.to: record removed or intent phase abandoned
preconditions: Any cleanup that changes operation_state follows the registry-mutex-serialized operation-state mutation protocol; expired-mutex removal or replacement remains an atomic mutex operation.
Expiry uses the contract clock rule.
A live lease is never stolen before expiresAt.
A mutating intent is never automatically removed; recovery must first fence the old generation and prove file-state safety.
effects: Any changed operation_state is atomically published with stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1.
Keep fencingGenerationHighWater at or above every generation ever issued.

x-shikin-safety-invariants.rule: For one databaseIdentity, active runtime leases have unique ownerId values; multiple different owners may coexist.
An operation state contains at most one exclusive restore/import intent.
Once exclusiveIntent is non-null, registration of every new runtime lease fails until the intent is released.
The short-lived record named registration_mutex is persisted separately, serializes every operation_state mutation, and grants no database mutation authority.

Registration, renewal, release, stale cleanup, exclusive-intent publication/phase change/cancellation/clear, and fencing high-water advance all follow x-shikin-operation-state-concurrency without exception.

Exclusive mutation begins only after every runtime lease has drained, complete journal evidence has been hash-verified before mutex acquisition, retained evidence has been revalidated under the mutex, and the commitment-bearing mutating state record is durably published.
fencingGenerationHighWater never decreases and every successful lease or intent acquisition receives a strictly greater generation.
Renewal, cancellation, mutation, completion, release, and stale recovery require the transition-specific owner, runtime, host, process, and fencing evidence.
An expired, released, abandoned, or superseded owner cannot authorize writes, rename database files, or publish completion.

Under the current revalidated registry mutex, lease/intent transitions, stateRevision = previous.stateRevision + 1, and fencing high-water updates are atomically persisted; partial records are invalid.

stateRevision.description: Monotonic operation-state revision; every successful mutation sets this to the post-acquisition previous value plus exactly one.

mutexId.description: Fresh owner nonce/token used to fence expired, removed, or superseded mutex holders.
